title.narrative: Market evidence, Analysis, and Provision of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance in the Gaza Strip

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Gaza Strip remains affected by extensive destruction, repeated displacement, and the breakdown of essential services. While the ceasefire in October 2025 has eased conditions marginally, households continue to face severely constrained incomes and limited access to basic goods and services. December 2025 IMPACT market assessment of 55 markets reports low to moderate functionality due to supply shortages, high transport costs, and infrastructure constraints. However, with 95% of vendors accepting cash and 80% e-wallet payments, MPCA remains a relevant modality when aligned with market conditions and complemented as needed by in-kind support. Acted PDM data from December 2025 confirms its effectiveness, with 99% of recipients purchasing priority items (96% for food, 53% for WASH, 26% for shelter needs). Acted’s late November 2025 data indicate that households continue to experience constrained access to key essentials, notably fresh food produce, shelter items, and fuel. In this context, Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) is critical for enabling the most vulnerable households to meet urgent needs, including food, hygiene items, child-related supplies, shelter and non-food items, transportation, and medical expenses, while supporting their resilience and dignity. ltbrgtDespite the essential role of cash assistance, gaps remain in the evidence available to support efficient operational decision-making. Humanitarian actors require timely, actionable insights to anticipate market disruptions, identify liquidity constraints, and understand both HH and vendor responses to shocks. Addressing these gaps means conducting quick, targeted assessments to track sudden market fluctuations, alongside comprehensive analysis of market functionality to understand underlying structural constraints, which is critical for maintaining the flexibility and effectiveness of MPCA in rapidly changing conditions. ltbrgtREACH with global expertise in evidence production, information management and humanitarian coordination, will aim to fill these gaps by combining systematic market analysis with on-demand market analysis, thereby supporting the Cash Working Group (CWG) and MPCA actors at large. Using its established vendor and consumer key informant networks in Gaza, the project will produce timely, location-specific insights and in-depth assessments of market functionality, liquidity, and supply chain dynamics, with information outputs including a market functionality report, multiple granular municipality-level market functionality maps, a comprehensive liquidity mapping report and risk analysis, and other ad-hoc products based on sectoral information needs. This evidence will directly support MPCA partners to plan and adapt assistance based on current market realities, anticipate emerging risks, and ensure that households can meet their prioritized needs without resorting to negative coping mechanisms. By providing flexible, actionable, and operationally relevant information, the project strengthens the effectiveness, timeliness, and responsiveness of MPCA. ltbrgtActed and ACAD will therefore provide one round of MPCA for eligible vulnerable HHs who have not yet received any support, ensuring access to essential needs and financial relief. The project will target ltbgt840lt/bgt vulnerable HHs (ltbgt4,620 individuals: 1,095 women, 1,183 girls, 924 PwDlt/bgt) across 4 governorates - Deir Al Balah, Khan Yunis, Gaza City and North Gaza, with one round of MPCA, amounting 1,250 ILS per household. The exact locations for distribution will be determined in coordination with community representatives and in response to the most urgent and evolving needs on the ground. Feedback from Acted’s recent cash intervention in November 2025 shows a very high level of beneficiary satisfaction, with over 99% of respondents satisfied with the assistance provided, underscoring the continued relevance, appropriateness, and effectiveness of MPCA as a response modality in the current, post-ceasefire context.ltbrgtlt/pgt
